items.title: Poonawalla Fincorp raises Rs 2,500 crore via QIP
items.description: In a remarkable move, Poonawalla Fincorp has secured ₹2,500 crore through a strategic qualified institutional placement. The company offered its equity shares to institutional investors at a price of ₹370.75 each, attracting a mix of domestic and international financial entities. As of the conclusion of Q3 FY26, Poonawalla Fincorp reported impressive assets under management totaling ₹55,017 crore.

items.title: ET Classroom: Rethinking returns in a volatile market
items.description: Equities may no longer solely drive portfolio returns due to slowing growth and high valuations. Investors should diversify across asset classes like debt, gold, and international equities to manage risk and achieve stable returns. Expectations should shift towards risk-adjusted returns, with 8-10% potentially being reasonable in the current volatile market.

items.title: Investors slash growth views by most in 4 years: BofA
items.description: Bank of America survey highlights a sharp downgrade in global growth outlook the steepest in four years as investor caution deepens.

items.title: Wall Street scales highs, oil drops on hopes for renewed US-Iran talks
items.description: Wall Street indexes advanced Tuesday as prospects for new U.S.-Iran peace talks emerged, pulling down oil prices and the U.S. dollar. The S&P 500 neared a record closing high, while Brent crude and WTI futures saw significant drops. Investors are optimistic about a potential de-escalation, despite ongoing inflation concerns.

items.title: D-Street gets a bit of momentum, don’t take it for long bounce
items.description: A recent rebound in benchmark indices has improved short-term market momentum, but it is not yet strong enough to signal a sustained bullish trend.The share of NSE’s top 500 stocks trading above their 50-day moving average rose to 49% from 18% during the peak of the West Asia conflict, nearing pre-war levels of 50.5%, indicating recovery but not full strength.

items.title: GIFT Nifty jumps over 300 pts, signals positive start; here's the trading setup
items.description: Indian markets saw a strong rebound after six weeks of decline, boosted by positive global sentiment. Hopes for a US-Iran ceasefire initially supported the rally. However, the collapse of peace talks and rising tensions led to market volatility. The Gift Nifty signals a positive start for Wednesday's trading session. Oil prices declined amid expectations of renewed peace talks.

items.title: Stocks in news: ICICI Pru Life, Anand Rathi Share, LIC, Vedanta, HAL
items.description: Markets experienced volatility, declining nearly 1% due to weak global cues, with analysts emphasizing the critical support level of 23,500 for a rebound. Several companies like ICICI Pru Life, Anand Rathi Share, LIC, Vedanta, and HAL are in focus due to Q4 results and news developments.
